title: Northwind Bank profits climb as interest income surges
content: Northwind Bank reported a 24% rise in annual profit on Tuesday, driven by higher interest rates across Europe. Chief executive Helena Marsh said the lender had benefited from strong mortgage demand in London and Manchester. Shares in the bank rose 3% in early trading. Analysts at Crestline Capital warned that margins could narrow next year if the central bank cuts rates. The bank also announced a share buyback worth £500 million.

title: Director Ava Linden wins best film award
content: Ava Linden's drama The Silent Harbour won best film at the European Film Awards in Berlin on Saturday. The film, about a fishing family in Norway, also collected awards for best actress and best screenplay. Linden thanked her cast and said the story was inspired by her grandmother. Actor Samuel Okoro won best actor for his role in the thriller Glass City. The ceremony was hosted by comedian Rosa Delgado.

title: Prime minister unveils plan to cut NHS waiting lists
content: The prime minister has unveiled a plan to cut NHS waiting lists by expanding community diagnostic centres. The government said £2 billion would be invested over three years. Health secretary Rachel Morgan said the plan would help patients get faster treatment. Opposition leader David Carter said the measures did not go far enough. Doctors' unions welcomed the funding but warned of staff shortages.

title: Harrington scores twice as United beat City
content: Striker Leo Harrington scored twice as United beat City 3-1 in the Premier League on Sunday. Harrington opened the scoring after ten minutes with a powerful header. City equalised before half-time but United dominated the second half. Manager Paul Evans praised his team's determination. The win lifts United to third in the table.

title: Startup Cognita unveils AI assistant for doctors
content: London startup Cognita has launched an artificial intelligence assistant that helps doctors write patient notes. The software uses speech recognition and a large language model to summarise consultations. Founder Amir Haddad said the tool could save doctors two hours a day. Trials in five NHS hospitals showed promising results. Privacy campaigners called for strict safeguards on patient data.

title: Retail sales fall for third month as shoppers cut back
content: UK retail sales fell for the third consecutive month in March, according to the Office for National Statistics. Clothing and furniture stores saw the steepest declines as households struggled with rising energy bills. Economist Priya Raman of Halden Research said consumer confidence remained fragile. Supermarkets fared better, with food sales broadly flat. The figures raise fears that the economy could slip into recession later this year.

title: Pop star Kira Vale announces world tour
content: Pop star Kira Vale has announced a 60-date world tour, starting in Los Angeles in September. The tour will visit cities including London, Paris, Tokyo and Sydney. Vale said fans could expect songs from her new album Neon Hearts alongside older hits. Tickets go on sale next week and are expected to sell out quickly. Her last tour broke attendance records at several stadiums.

title: Election campaign enters final week
content: The general election campaign has entered its final week with polls showing a tight race between the two main parties. Leaders are touring marginal seats in Wales and the Midlands. The economy and immigration remain the top issues for voters, according to a survey by Northbridge Polling. Smaller parties are hoping to win seats in Scotland. Voters go to the polls next Thursday.

title: Tennis star Sofia Ricci wins Wimbledon title
content: Italy's Sofia Ricci has won her first Wimbledon title after beating the defending champion in three sets. The 22-year-old recovered from losing the first set to win 4-6 6-3 6-2. Ricci said winning at Wimbledon was a childhood dream. She becomes the first Italian woman to win the singles title. Her coach Marco Bellini said she had worked incredibly hard.

title: Smartphone maker Pixelon launches foldable phone
content: Smartphone maker Pixelon has launched its first foldable phone, priced at $1,499. The device features a seven-inch screen that folds in half and a new high-speed processor. Product chief Yuki Tanaka said the phone was the thinnest foldable on the market. Reviewers praised the display but criticised battery life. The phone goes on sale in the US, Japan and Europe next month.

title: Oil prices jump after supply cuts announced
content: Oil prices rose sharply on Monday after major producers agreed to extend output cuts until the end of the year. Brent crude climbed 6% to its highest level since January. Energy firms including Meridian Petroleum saw their share prices rally. Airlines were among the biggest fallers on the stock market amid worries over fuel costs. Analysts expect petrol prices in Germany and France to increase within weeks.

title: Streaming series breaks viewing records
content: Fantasy series The Iron Crown has become the most-watched show in the history of streaming service Flixora. More than 90 million households watched the first season within four weeks of its release. Showrunner Daniel Hart said the cast and crew were overwhelmed by the response. A second season has already been commissioned and will film in Ireland. Critics praised the show's visual effects and performances.

title: Parliament votes on new immigration bill
content: MPs have voted in favour of a new immigration bill that will change the rules for work visas. The bill passed by 312 votes to 270 after a heated debate in the House of Commons. Home secretary James Whitfield said the reforms would make the system fairer. Critics argued the changes would harm businesses facing labour shortages. The bill now moves to the House of Lords.

title: England name squad for Six Nations
content: England head coach Steve Barnes has named a 36-man squad for the upcoming Six Nations championship. Uncapped winger Jamal Brooks is among five new faces. Captain Owen Price returns after recovering from a knee injury. England open their campaign against Scotland at Twickenham in February. Barnes said the squad blended experience with exciting young talent.

title: Cyber attack hits major hospital network
content: A cyber attack has disrupted computer systems at a major hospital network in the United States. Hackers used ransomware to encrypt files and demanded payment in cryptocurrency. Some operations were postponed and ambulances were diverted to other hospitals. Security expert Nina Volkova said healthcare was an increasingly common target. The FBI is investigating the attack.

title: Carmaker Voltaro to cut 2,000 jobs in restructuring
content: Electric carmaker Voltaro plans to cut 2,000 jobs as part of a major restructuring aimed at reducing costs. The company said demand for its vehicles in China had slowed sharply this year. Chief financial officer Marcus Lindqvist said the cuts would save about $400 million annually. Unions in Sweden criticised the decision and called for talks. Voltaro shares fell 8% following the announcement.

title: Theatre revival of classic musical opens to rave reviews
content: A revival of the musical Starlight Avenue opened in London's West End to glowing reviews. Critics praised lead actress Molly Brennan's powerful vocals and the lavish staging. Director Julian Price said he wanted to introduce the show to a new generation. The production has already extended its run until next spring. Ticket sales have reportedly topped £10 million.

title: Foreign ministers meet to discuss trade deal
content: Foreign ministers from the UK and Canada met in Ottawa to discuss a new trade agreement. The deal would reduce tariffs on food, cars and financial services. Foreign secretary Laura Bennett said talks had been constructive. Canadian officials said several issues, including agriculture, remain unresolved. Both governments hope to sign an agreement by the end of the year.

title: Marathon record broken in Berlin
content: Kenyan runner David Kiprono broke the marathon world record in Berlin on Sunday, finishing in two hours, 34 seconds. Kiprono ran much of the race alone after his pacemakers dropped out. He said perfect weather conditions had helped him. Ethiopia's Tadesse Bekele finished second. In the women's race, Grace Wanjiru won in a course record time.

title: Social network Chirpr faces fine over data breach
content: Social network Chirpr has been fined €200 million by European regulators over a data breach affecting 50 million users. The Irish Data Protection Commission said the company failed to protect personal information. Chirpr said it would appeal the decision. The breach exposed email addresses and phone numbers. It is one of the largest privacy fines ever issued in Europe.

title: Inflation eases to lowest level in two years
content: Inflation in the eurozone fell to 2.4% in April, its lowest level in two years, official data showed. Lower energy prices and cheaper food helped ease pressure on household budgets. The European Central Bank is now widely expected to cut interest rates in June. Economist Tomas Berger said businesses were seeing costs stabilise. However, services inflation remained stubbornly high.

title: Veteran actor Leonard Shaw dies aged 88
content: Veteran actor Leonard Shaw, best known for his role in the detective series Moorland, has died aged 88. His family said he died peacefully at home in Edinburgh. Shaw's career spanned six decades on stage, film and television. Fellow actors paid tribute to his warmth, humour and generosity. He won a lifetime achievement award from the British Academy in 2015.

title: Minister resigns over expenses row
content: Transport minister Colin Hayes has resigned following a row over his parliamentary expenses. An investigation found he had claimed thousands of pounds for a second home he rarely used. Hayes said he had made mistakes but denied any wrongdoing. The prime minister accepted his resignation and appointed Sarah Lin as his replacement. Opposition parties called for a review of the expenses system.

title: Cricket team collapses on opening day of Test
content: England collapsed to 145 all out on the opening day of the first Test against India in Mumbai. Spin bowler Ravi Menon took six wickets as batsmen struggled on a turning pitch. Only Joe Hartley offered resistance with a battling 52. India closed the day on 88 for two in reply. Captain Ben Foster admitted his side had batted poorly.

title: Quantum computer achieves new milestone
content: Researchers at Qubitron have built a quantum computer with 1,000 stable qubits, a major milestone for the technology. The company said the machine solved a chemistry problem that would take classical computers years. Chief scientist Dr Elena Petrova said practical applications were now within reach. Experts cautioned that error rates remain a challenge. The system will be available to researchers through the cloud.

title: Airline Skyvale reports record summer bookings
content: Budget airline Skyvale said summer bookings had hit a record high, with flights to Spain and Greece in strong demand. The company raised its full-year profit forecast by 15%. Chief executive Dana Kowalski said customers were prioritising holidays despite the cost of living squeeze. Fuel costs and air traffic control delays remain risks. Skyvale shares gained 5% on the London stock exchange.

title: Music festival line-up revealed
content: Organisers of the Riverside Festival have revealed this year's line-up, with rock band The Hollow Kings headlining on Saturday. Rapper Jaylen Cross and singer Mira Solano will also perform. The three-day event in Somerset is expected to attract 150,000 fans. Festival director Karen Walsh said the line-up was the most diverse in its history. Tickets sold out within hours of going on sale.

title: Council tax set to rise across England
content: Most councils in England are set to raise council tax by the maximum 5% allowed from April. Local authorities said rising demand for social care had put their budgets under severe strain. The Local Government Association warned some councils faced bankruptcy without more funding. Ministers said they had increased support for local government. Households face an average increase of around £100 a year.

title: Formula One champion signs new contract
content: Formula One world champion Lucas Moreau has signed a new three-year contract with the Apex Racing team. The French driver has won two championships since joining the team in 2021. Team principal Karl Weber said Moreau was the best driver on the grid. The deal is reported to be worth more than $50 million a year. Moreau leads this season's championship by 30 points.

title: Electric vehicle charging network expands
content: Charging company VoltGrid will install 10,000 rapid chargers across Europe over the next three years. The chargers can add 200 miles of range in about 15 minutes. Chief executive Rafael Ortiz said the network would ease drivers' range anxiety. The investment is backed by a €1 billion loan from the European Investment Bank. Most chargers will be located at motorway service stations.

title: Tech giant's takeover of chip designer approved by regulators
content: Competition regulators have approved Orbitex's $12 billion takeover of chip designer Lumen Circuits. The deal had faced scrutiny over concerns it would reduce competition in the semiconductor market. Orbitex agreed to license key patents to rivals as a condition of approval. Investors welcomed the decision, sending Lumen shares up 11%. The merger is expected to complete by the end of the quarter.

title: Box office hit sequel tops charts again
content: Animated sequel Forest Friends 2 topped the box office for a third straight weekend, taking $85 million worldwide. The film has now earned more than $600 million globally. Studio Silverlight Pictures said it had become its most successful animated release. Voice actor Tessa Monroe returns as the lead character Pip. A third film is already in development.

title: Opposition leader sets out policy on housing
content: Opposition leader David Carter has promised to build 1.5 million homes if his party wins the next election. Speaking in Leeds, he said young people had been locked out of home ownership. The plans include reforms to planning rules and new towns across England. Government ministers said the pledge was unrealistic and uncosted. Housing charities welcomed the focus on affordable homes.

title: Olympic swimmer wins third gold medal
content: Swimmer Emma Lawson won her third gold medal of the Olympic Games with victory in the 200m freestyle. The Australian touched the wall in an Olympic record time. American Chloe Hayes took silver and Canada's Maya Singh won bronze. Lawson said she was exhausted but thrilled. She will compete in the relay final on Saturday.

title: Games console sales smash forecasts
content: Sales of the new Nova games console have smashed forecasts, with 10 million units sold in three months. Maker Arcadia Interactive said demand had outstripped supply in many countries. The console's exclusive game, Starbound, has sold 5 million copies. Analyst Chris Palmer said the console had the strongest launch in industry history. Arcadia raised its annual sales target.

title: Housing market shows signs of recovery
content: House prices rose for the second month in a row in May, suggesting the property market may be stabilising. The average price of a home in England rose 0.8% to £285,000, according to lender Harbourline. Mortgage approvals also increased as borrowing costs dipped. Estate agent Oliver Grant said buyer interest in Birmingham and Leeds had picked up. Economists cautioned that affordability remains stretched.

title: Author's debut novel wins literary prize
content: First-time novelist Nadia Hussain has won the Harwood Prize for fiction with her book The Salt Road. The novel follows three generations of a family travelling from Morocco to France. Judges called it a moving and beautifully written debut. Hussain receives £30,000 and said she was stunned to win. Sales of the book are expected to soar following the award.

title: Scottish parliament debates independence referendum
content: The Scottish parliament has debated a motion calling for a second independence referendum. First minister Fiona Grant said Scotland should have the right to choose its future. Unionist parties argued that voters wanted a focus on public services instead. The motion was passed but has no legal force without Westminster's agreement. Polls suggest Scots remain evenly divided on the issue.

title: Rovers sack manager after poor run
content: Championship club Rovers have sacked manager Tony Walsh after a run of seven games without a win. The club sits in the relegation zone after 20 matches. Chairman Richard Hale said the decision had been difficult. Assistant coach Mark Lewis will take charge on an interim basis. Rovers face a crucial match against fellow strugglers on Saturday.

title: Government plans new rules for artificial intelligence
content: The government has published plans for new rules governing the use of artificial intelligence. Developers of powerful AI models will have to test them for safety before release. Technology secretary Priya Shah said the rules would balance innovation and protection. Tech companies broadly welcomed the approach but asked for clarity. The rules will be overseen by a new AI safety office.

title: Coffee chain Brewhaus expands into Asia
content: Coffee chain Brewhaus plans to open 300 stores across Japan, South Korea and Singapore over the next five years. The company said rising demand for premium coffee in Asia made the region its top growth priority. Founder Lena Fischer said each new store would create around 20 jobs. The expansion will be funded through a new $250 million bond issue. Brewhaus currently operates 1,200 stores worldwide.

title: Comedian announces return to stand-up
content: Comedian Pete Morrison will return to stand-up comedy next year after a five-year break. His new show, Still Here, will tour 40 venues across the UK and Ireland. Morrison said he had missed performing live in front of audiences. The comedian stepped back from touring to focus on his television work. Tickets for the Dublin shows have already sold out.

title: EU leaders agree climate targets at summit
content: European Union leaders meeting in Brussels have agreed to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 70% by 2040. The deal came after all-night negotiations at the summit. Poland and Hungary secured extra funding to help their coal-reliant regions. Commission president Anja Sorensen called it a historic moment for Europe. Environmental groups said the targets still fell short of what scientists recommend.

title: Golfer claims first major championship
content: Irish golfer Conor Byrne claimed his first major championship with a dramatic victory at the Open. Byrne holed a long birdie putt on the final green to win by one shot. American Tyler Reed finished second after leading for much of the final round. Byrne said the win meant everything to him and his family. He moves into the world's top ten.

title: Satellite internet service launches in rural areas
content: Satellite internet company Skylink has begun offering broadband to rural communities in Scotland and Wales. The service offers download speeds of up to 200 megabits per second. Many remote villages previously had no access to fast broadband. Customer Jean Mackay said the service had transformed her small business. The company plans to launch 3,000 more satellites next year.

title: Stock markets rally on strong jobs data
content: Stock markets in New York and London rallied on Friday after US jobs data came in stronger than expected. Employers added 280,000 jobs in May while unemployment held steady at 3.9%. The Dow Jones index rose 1.2% and the FTSE 100 hit a record high. Bond yields climbed as investors scaled back expectations of rate cuts. Analysts said the economy was proving more resilient than feared.

title: Film festival celebrates independent cinema
content: The Lakeshore Film Festival opened on Thursday with a record 250 independent films on the programme. Festival director Ines Moreau said the event would champion new voices in cinema. The opening film, a documentary about jazz musicians in New Orleans, received a standing ovation. Awards will be announced at a gala ceremony next week. More than 40,000 visitors are expected.

title: Government announces review of voting age
content: The government has announced a review into lowering the voting age to 16 for general elections. Constitution minister Ben Ashford said young people deserved a greater say in politics. Sixteen-year-olds can already vote in Scottish and Welsh elections. Some Conservative MPs said the change was unnecessary. The review is expected to report within twelve months.

title: Boxer retains heavyweight title
content: Heavyweight champion Marcus Cole retained his world title with a unanimous points victory in Las Vegas. Cole dominated the fight against challenger Viktor Petrov over 12 rounds. The 31-year-old British boxer remains unbeaten in 28 professional fights. Promoter Frank Doyle said a unification bout could take place next year. Cole said he wanted to fight the best in the division.

title: Chipmaker unveils faster processor for laptops
content: Chipmaker Silica Systems has unveiled a new processor for laptops that it says is 40% faster than its predecessor. The chip also uses less power, extending battery life by up to five hours. Engineering chief Rahul Mehta said the design used a new three-nanometre manufacturing process. Laptops using the chip will go on sale in the autumn. Rivals are expected to respond with their own new processors.

title: Supermarket group Freshway posts profit warning
content: Supermarket group Freshway has warned that annual profits will fall short of expectations after a price war with discount rivals. The company said it had cut prices on more than 1,000 products to retain customers. Chief executive Graham Doyle said the investment was necessary to protect market share. Freshway shares slumped 14%. The retailer employs 90,000 staff across Britain and Ireland.

title: Rock band reunites for anniversary album
content: Rock band Echo Valley has reunited to record an album marking 25 years since their debut. Singer Tom Reilly said the band had put past disagreements behind them. The album, Return to Echo Valley, will be released in October. The group will also play a series of concerts in London, Manchester and Glasgow. Fans reacted with excitement on social media.

title: Senate passes defence spending bill
content: The US Senate has passed a $850 billion defence spending bill after weeks of negotiations. The bill includes funding for new ships, aircraft and a pay rise for troops. Senator Maria Alvarez said the measure would strengthen national security. Some lawmakers opposed the bill, arguing that the money should be spent on healthcare. The president is expected to sign it into law.

title: Basketball team clinches championship
content: The Harbor City Hawks won the basketball championship with a 108-101 victory in game seven of the finals. Point guard Andre Mitchell scored 38 points and was named most valuable player. It is the Hawks' first title in 25 years. Coach Lisa Grant said her players had shown remarkable resilience. Thousands of fans celebrated in the streets overnight.

title: Open source software project hits milestone
content: The open source database project OpenStore has reached 100,000 contributors worldwide. The software is used by thousands of companies to manage their data. Project lead Sara Lindgren said the community had grown rapidly over the past year. Volunteers from more than 150 countries have contributed code. The project recently released a major update with improved security features.

title: Shipping costs soar as trade routes disrupted
content: The cost of shipping goods from Asia to Europe has more than doubled in a month as vessels avoid disrupted trade routes. Container rates reached their highest level since the pandemic, according to freight analyst Kai Nakamura. Retailers warned customers could face delays and higher prices. Shipping firm Bluewave Logistics said journeys were taking up to two weeks longer. Manufacturers in Italy and Germany reported shortages of components.

title: TV talent show crowns new winner
content: Singer Grace Adeyemi has been crowned the winner of television talent show Star Search after a nail-biting final. The 19-year-old from Birmingham won a recording contract and £100,000. More than 8 million viewers watched the live final on Saturday night. Judge Carla Benson said Adeyemi had a rare and special voice. Her debut single will be released next month.

title: Local elections deliver blow to governing party
content: The governing party has suffered heavy losses in local elections across England, losing control of 12 councils. Opposition parties and independents made significant gains in the south. Party chairman Nigel Frost admitted it had been a difficult night. Political analyst Hannah Webb said the results reflected voter frustration with the economy. The prime minister insisted the party could recover before the general election.

title: Cyclist wins Tour stage in the Alps
content: Belgian cyclist Pieter Janssens won a gruelling mountain stage of the Tour de France in the Alps. Janssens attacked on the final climb and held off his rivals to win by 40 seconds. Race leader Tomas Novak finished safely in the main group to keep the yellow jersey. Several riders crashed on a wet descent earlier in the stage. The race reaches Paris next Sunday.

title: Robot delivery trial begins in city centre
content: Delivery robots have begun bringing groceries to homes in Milton Keynes as part of a new trial. The six-wheeled robots travel on pavements and can carry up to three bags of shopping. Company RoboDrop said the robots had completed 5,000 deliveries in the first month. Residents said the service was convenient but some complained about robots blocking paths. The firm hopes to expand the trial to other cities.
